No, you cannot place the order [1][3]. 

Effective 1 September 2026 under AMD-SUP-2026-02 (which replaced POL-SUP-003 §4.4), Northbridge Cycles accepts a UN 38.3 certificate only if it was issued within the last 12 months and remains valid for at least 60 days after the order placement date [1][2][3]. 

Under the older, superseded rule, certificates issued within 24 months were accepted [1][3]. However, for any new orders placed from 1 September 2026, certificates meeting only the old 24-month rule count as no certificate in Ledgerline, which blocks new order placement [1][3]. Because the certificate was issued 18 months ago, it does not meet the current 12-month requirement [1][3].

NOT IN THE DOCUMENTS. The provided sources contain no information regarding Brightcell Energy, including their supplier onboarding or active status, existing rate contracts, or UN 38.3 certificate details.

No [2]. Under POL-PUR-001 Clause 6, a cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not justify switching suppliers for a lithium-cell part [2]. 

Purchasers must prefer suppliers with current rate contracts [2]. Additionally, before placing orders with a new supplier, the supplier must be formally onboarded under POL-SUP-003 [2]. Any supplier of lithium-cell parts (including battery packs) must hold a verified, unexpired UN 38.3 certificate in Ledgerline that was issued within the last 12 months and is valid for at least 60 days after the purchase order date [1][2][3].

Under AMD-SUP-2026-02 (effective 1 September 2026, amending POL-SUP-003 §4.4), a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if it was issued within the last 12 months [1][2][3]. In addition, its valid-to date must extend at least 60 days beyond the date the purchase order is placed [1][2][3]. Certificates issued under the superseded 24-month rule now count as no certificate and prevent new order placement [1][2].

**Who checks it:**
- **Purchase staff:** Must check the certificate's issue date and valid-to date against the rule before raising an order [2].
- **Ledgerline ERP:** Automatically enforces order blocking; an expired or invalid certificate counts as no certificate, preventing order placement [1].
- **Senior Buyer:** Runs the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) on the first working day of each month with a 90-day lookahead window to identify and contact suppliers with expiring UN 38.3 certificates [1][2][5].
